Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and for the forecast. Copying Sales Ops (Priyom) and Pricing (Kim) to confirm numbers.

Quick summary while they pull the spreadsheet:
- We can do quarterly and annual commits. Annual gives the best blended unit price (roughly 18–22% lower vs month-to-month for your forecast levels).
- SLA stacking (availability band + priority response window) is additive but we offer a bundled discount when both are purchased for >=12 months. That bundle is what unlocks the onboarding credit.
- Escalation coverage: standard included hours are M-F 9–6 PST; extended oncall (24/7 triage) is an add-on, priced as either a flat retainer or as a blended per-hour uplift.

I attached a one-page example (SLA_Tiers) and a short proposal I think will match your ask. Priyom / Kim — can you confirm the one-time onboarding credit and an illustrative quote for Brightline at the forecasted volumes?

Next step: if the numbers look good, I can put a proposal into DocuSign and loop legal for a PO.

Hi all — pulled preliminary numbers and a proposed concession. Notes: 

1) Commit tiers
- Quarterly commit (Q): baseline price = $0.018/token; annual commit (A): baseline price = $0.014/token (approx -22%).

2) SLA stacking bundle (A, 12 months min)
- Availability band (99.9% standard -> 99.95% premium) = +6% list uplift
- Priority response window (4-hour -> 1-hour) = +9% list uplift
- Bundled discount when both (A, 12-month) = -10% off combined uplift (net effect: ~+4.5% vs baseline annual).

3) Escalation coverage
- 24/7 triage retainer: flat $12,500/mo or equivalent 2.4% gross uplift on forecasted usage (choose whichever is contractually simpler)

4) Onboarding credit
- For a 12-month annual commit we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 (applied to first invoice) if the customer commits to the SLA bundle.

5) Example summary (based on Brightline forecast attached):
- Annual commit + SLA bundle + 24/7 retainer => blended unit approx $0.0147/token after credit amortization across year (illustrative).

Caveats: these numbers assume pinned model family (no model-hopping) and no extraordinary regional failover costs. If Brightline wants a regional DR guarantee (multi-region active/active) that's a separate shelf item.

Logan — if you want, I can convert the above into a compact quote table (CSV) for procurement and add a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Best,
Priyom Das

Agree with Priyom's numbers. A couple of product clarifications to set expectations for procurement: 

- The "priority response window" applies to triage/first-response (acknowledgement and initial mitigation guidance). Incident resolution SLAs are incident dependent and scope-defined in the SOW.
- Onboarding credit applies only if the SOW includes our standard enablement package (kickoff, runbook transfer, dedicated TPM for 4 weeks). If Brightline reduces enablement scope, the credit is pro-rated.

Logan: small negotiation play — if Brightline signs an M + 36-month runway (annual invoicing, 3-year term) we can increase the onboarding credit to $40k and add a single quarter of waived retainer (first quarter free) for the 24/7 triage. That may be attractive if finance is looking for CAPEX smoothing.

Kim
